title: How much did global average temperature exceed pre-industrial levels in 2024?

sources.title: 2024 - a second record-breaking year, following the ...
sources.snippet: 2024 saw unprecedented global temperatures, following on from the remarkable warmth of 2023. It also became the first year with an average temperature clearly exceeding 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level – a threshold set by the Paris Agreement to significantly reduce the risks and impacts of climate change.

answer: In 2024, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) put the global average temperature at 1.60°C above an estimate of the pre-industrial level [2]. C3S also recorded the global average temperature as 15.10°C [2]. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) confirmed 2024 as the warmest year on record at about 1.55°C above the 1850–1900 average, with a margin of uncertainty of ±0.13°C [3]. NASA estimated that 2024 was about 1.47°C warmer than the 1850–1900 average [4]. NOAA’s annual report put the 2024 global average surface temperature 1.46°C above the pre-industrial average [5]. These figures differ because the organisations use different datasets and methods; WMO’s figure comes from a consolidated analysis of six international datasets [3], while NOAA uses its own record [5]. All of them place 2024 above the 1.5°C threshold for a single calendar year [2][3][4].
